4. Accordingly, Kotwali Police Station Case No. 39 dated 17-12-2003 under sections 406/4091420 of the Penal Code was recorded against those  six accused persons. During investigation of the case accused Fariduddin, made a confessional statement implicating himself and other accused persons, including the petitioner, with the accusation of defalcation of the aforesaid money. After investigation of the case on 29-10-2004 the police of Kotwali police station of Sylhet, submitted final report against four accused namely, (1) Kaisar-uz-zaman (petitioner), (2) Nasrin Chowdhury, (3) Ahmed' Chowdhury and (4) Nasiruddin and charge sheet against two accused namely, (5) Farid uddin and (6) Iqbal uddin. The learned Magistrate concerned accepted such police report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and sent the case to the Sessions Judge, Sylhet, who at first registered the  case as a Sessions Case. Subsequently, on 12-3- 2005 he as the Senior Special Judge, Sylhet, took cognizance of the offences against Farid uddin, Iqbal uddin and Kaisar-uz-zaman (petitioner) under the sections 406/409/420 of the Penal Code and discharged accused Nasrin Chowdhury, Ahmed Chowdhury and Nasiruddin. The case was registered as Special Case No.1 of2005, pending in the Court of Senior Special Judge, consisting of the Sessions Judge, Sylhet. For quashing the proceeding of that special case, so far as it relates to the petitioner him on the grounds, (1) the proceeding of the case is abuse of rocess of the Court as cognizance of the offences against those accused persons was taken by the Senior Special Judge without sanction of the Government or Durniti Daman Commission and (2) that a money suit has already been filed by the bank against those accused persons for realization of the money allegedly defalcated, the petitioner moved this Court filing an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained this Rule. 

 5. Mr AS Md Mubin the learned Advocate appearing on the behalf of the petitioner supports the Rule. He submits that the petitioner .was the Manager of IFIC Bank, Tultikar branch, Co-accused Farid uddin was the cashier of the same bank. They allegedly committed offence of criminal breach of  trust punishable under section 409 of the Penal Code, which is specified in the schedule of Criminal  Law Amendment Act, 1958 and the Dumiti Daman  Commission Ain, 2004 (hereinafter referred as the  Ain). Section 20 of the Ain provides that investigation of the offences under the Ain and also the offences under other laws specified in the schedule  of the Ain are to be done by the Dumiti Daman  Commission (hereinafter called the Commission) or any officer of the Commission authorized by the  commission to hold investigation section 32 of the  Ain provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, or any  other law in force, no Court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Ain without the sanction of the  Commission. The investigating officer, after completion of investigation of any offence under the Ain, before submission of report in the Court must obtain sanction of the Commission and a copy of such sanction must be submitted to the Court with investigation report. In the instant case, which is of an offence under section 409 of the Penal Code and included the schedule of the Ain, the investigation was 'done neither by the Commission nor by any authorized officer of the Commission and no prior sanction of the Commission was obtained. He further submits that section 6(5) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act (hereinafter referred as the Act) provides that prior sanction of the Government is  required to prosecute a public servant for any  offence under the schedule of this Act. If the petition of complaint or the police report is not accompanied  by such sanction, the Special Judge shall immediately on receipt of the complaint or report address  the Government in the matter by a letter. An offences under section 409 of the Penal Code committed by public servant being an offence included in the schedule of the Act is exclusively triable by the Special Judge in accordance with the Act. But in the instant case the Senior Special Judge, Sylhet, took cognizance of the offence against the petitioner and two other accused persons without prior sanction of the Government, who had no jurisdiction to take cognizance of the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code, allegedly committed by the petitioner, as a public servant without prior sanction of the Government. So the order of taking cognizance of the offences against the petitioner in this case is without lawful authority and, as such, the entire case has been vitiated for lack of jurisdiction. In this regard he refers the case of Abdur Rahman vs State 48 DLR (AD) 167. Thus according to Mr Mubin continuation of the proceeding of the present case is abuse of the process of the Court, to prevent which the same should be quashed. " 

 8. Mr Ashique submits that in accordance with the Criminal Law Amendment Act, the offence under section 409 of the Penal Code allegedly committed by the petitioner, who was a public servant, as the Manager of IFIC Bank, Tultikar branch, is exclusively cognizable and triable by the Special Judge. Accordingly on 12-3-2005 the Senior Special Judge, Sylhet, rightly took cognizance of the offence against the petitioner. Sub-section (5) of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 was omitted on 18-7-2004. At the time of taking cognizance of the offence against the petitioner by the Senior Special Judge, Sylhet, the provision of taking prior sanction of the Government before taking cognizance of the offence was non-existent. So there was no legal necessary for taking sanction of the Government before taking cognizance of the offence in this case and, as such, there was no non- compliance of law of prior sanction. He further submits that Durniti Daman Commission Ain (here- in after referred as the Ain) came into force on 9-5-2004, The present case was started with the Lodging of FIR on 17-12-2003 and after investigation police submitted report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 29-10-2004. So in the instant case question of holding investigation by the Durniti Daman Commission or any authorized officer of the commission as provided in section 20 .of the Ain and of taking sanction of the Commission before taking cognizance as required under section 32 of the Ain does not arise. The provisions of those two sections of the Ain have no manner of application in the instant case as it was at the later stage of investigation when the Ain came into operation. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2 adds that the instant case will proceed in accordance with the Ain and Durniti Daman Commission Bidhimala, 2007, framed under the Ain, which is a procedural law, having retrospective effect. Under Sub-Rule (5) of Rule 15 of the Durniti Daman Commission Bidhimala, 2007, the learned Special Judge is to address the Chairman of the Durniti Daman Commission for sanction and if so addressed, the Commission under sub-rule (3) of rule of the Bidhimala will accord sanction, As prima-facie case under section 409 of the Penal Code has been made out against the petitioner, he must be tried under the present law of the country and should not be allowed to go without trial. In this regard Mr Rubait refers the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, 63 DLR (AD) 18. Thus according to the learned Advocate for the opposite party No.2 the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. As it is a case of offence under section 409 of the Penal Code committed by the officers of a bank, who under section 110 of the Bank Companies Act, 1991, are public servant, exclusively cognizance and triable by the Special Judge under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The learned Magistrate, who by the order dated 3-11-2004, accepted the police report, had no jurisdiction to accept the police report and take cognizance of the offence against two accused persons and discharge remaining four accused including the petitioner as recommended by the police. (vide 39 DLR 412). 

 12. An offence punishable under section 409 of the Penal Code committed by a public servant in discharging his duty as public servant is still specified under the schedule of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 as before even after amendment of the schedule by Act XXII of 2004 on 18-7-2004. Section 5(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 provides that the offences specified in the schedule of the Act shall be triable exclusively by a Special Judge. Section 4 of the Act provides that a Special Judge may take cognizance of any offence triable under this Act upon receipt of complaint of facts which constitute such offence or upon a report in writing of such facts made by any police officer. An offence under section 409 of the Penal Code committed by a public servant in discharging his official duty as a public servant being specified in the schedule of the Act is triable exclusively by a Special Judge. Cognizance of such offence is to be taken by the Special Judge on a petition of complaint or on a police report submitted under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the instant case on the police report submitted under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Senior Special Judge took cognizance of the offence against the petitioner, through in the police report he was recommended to be discharged, and against two other accused namely, Farid uddin and Iqbal Ahmed, against whom charge sheet was submitted and discharged three other accused persons against whom final report was submitted. The Senior Special Judge is not bound by the recommendation of the police to discharge the accused against whom final report has been submitted. He is empowered under section 4(1) of the Act to take cognizance of the offence on the police report. Final report is also police report. In this regard the case of Abdus Salam Master vs State 36 DLR (AD) 58 may readily be referred, wherein it is held,- 

 "In the present case also the Special Judge can take cognizance against the petitioner under section 4 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 on the basis of trial report of the police." 

 17. Now the question is whether the Senior Special Judge acted illegally taking cognizance of the offence against the petitioner without prior sanction of the Government as provided in sub-section (5) of section 6 of the Act, which provides that notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure or any other law, previous sanction of the Government shall be required for the prosecution of a public servant for an Offence under the Act. It is further provided in the proviso to sub-section (5) of section 6 of the Act that in cases where the complaint or police report referred to in sub-section (1) of section 4 is not accompanied by such sanction of the Government the Special Judge shall immediately on receipt of the complaint or police report address by letter the Government in the matter and if the required sanction is neither received nor refused within sixty days of the receipt of the letter by the Government such sanction shall be deemed to have been duly accorded. 

 19. Sub-section (5) of section 6 of the Act was omitted on 18-5-2004 by Act No. XXII of 2004. In the instant case on 12-3-2005 when the Senior Special Judge took cognizance of the offence against the petitioner subsection (5) of section 6 of the Act was not in existence. After investigation, the police submitted report under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 29-10-2004. During investigation of the case section 6 (5) of the Act was omitted. Thus at the time of submission of police report on 29-10-2004 prior sanction of the Government for prosecuting the accused was not required under the law in existence. So taking cognizance of the offence against the petitioner without sanction of the Government is not illegal or without lawful authority.
